status_summary: No proposal to split CDC into separate data-publishing and public health policy agencies was found as of 2026-10-08. HHS announced a different restructuring on 2025-03-27: about 10,000 job cuts department-wide, a proposed Administration for a Healthy America (AHA) combining several agencies, and the preparedness office (ASPR) moving into CDC; CDC's chief operating officer put the net CDC staff reduction at 24 percent by June 2025. Nineteen states and the District of Columbia challenged the restructuring in New York v. Kennedy (D.R.I., Judge DuBose), and on 2025-07-01 the court granted a preliminary injunction, finding the states likely to succeed on claims that HHS acted arbitrarily and capriciously and contrary to law in disrupting congressionally mandated functions; the First Circuit denied the government's emergency stay request on 2025-09-17, the government voluntarily dismissed its appeal about six weeks later, and on 2026-04-07 the court denied a motion to dismiss the amended complaint. Congress did not fund AHA in the fiscal year 2026 Labor-HHS appropriation (Division B of Public Law 119-75, approved 2026-02-03, the day the House passed it 217 to 214 after Senate passage 71 to 29, per the Senate Appropriations Committee majority), as Fierce Healthcare reported on 2026-04-03, and a Holland & Knight alert says the proposed HHS reorganization was not included in the final funding package. The fiscal year 2027 request (Budget in Brief released 2026-04-03) repeats the approach: CDC budget authority of $5.280 billion versus $5.764 billion for fiscal year 2026 (a $484 million reduction), a new National Center for Chemicals and Toxins inside CDC, several CDC programs moved to AHA, and a cross-reference in the CDC chapter to the Office of Strategy chapter for the National Center for Health Statistics. The CDC chapter of the Budget in Brief refers readers to the Office of Strategy chapter for the National Center for Health Statistics, and an unverified lead from a post by the American Statistical Association (an association page, 2026-04-03) says HHS's justification proposes moving the center from CDC to a to-be-created Office of Strategy with $175 million, at low confidence because the Budget in Brief text read gave no center-level breakdown; this is the only element found that points toward separating a data function from CDC, and it is a budget proposal that does not create an agency with a legal duty to publish state-sourced data. Erica Schwartz was confirmed as CDC director on 2026-08-05.

timeline.event: S. 999, the Public Health Improvement Act, is introduced in the Senate and referred to the HELP Committee; it would limit CDC's objectives to communicable diseases, remove HHS discretion over communicable disease measures and move eight offices from CDC to NIH, without creating a separate data-publishing agency.

HHS announces a department restructuring: roughly 10,000 full-time positions cut, 28 divisions consolidated to 15, a new Administration for a Healthy America (combining the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health, HRSA, SAMHSA, ATSDR and NIOSH), and ASPR moved to CDC.
Government Executive reports CDC has shed about one quarter of its staff, net of about 800 reduction-in-force notices rescinded from roughly 2,400 issued in April 2025.

In New York v. Kennedy (D.R.I. No. 25-cv-196; 19 states and the District of Columbia) the court grants a preliminary injunction against parts of HHS's 2025-03-27 restructuring, finding the states likely to succeed on claims that HHS acted arbitrarily and capriciously and contrary to law, and that the announcement and resulting reduction-in-force notices were reviewable final agency action; the components at issue include CDC laboratory services, the Division of Reproductive Health, NIOSH, the National Center for Environmental Health and HIV, STD and TB prevention. The court makes no separate finding about AHA. Bloomberg Law reported on 2025-07-18 that the court declined to lift the injunction and denied a stay pending appeal.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island (via govinfo)

timeline.event: The House passes the final FY2026 Labor-HHS bill 217 to 214, after Senate passage 71 to 29, sending it to the President, per the Senate Appropriations Committee majority release of the same day; Fierce Healthcare later reported that Congress did not grant the request to fund the Administration for a Healthy America for FY2026.
timeline.source: U.S. Senate Committee on Appropriations (majority); Fierce Healthcare

timeline.event: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75, H.R. 7148) is approved on 2026-02-03; Division B is the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education appropriations act. The text of Division B could not be read; the statement that it does not fund AHA rests on a Fierce Healthcare report of 2026-04-03 and a Holland & Knight alert of 2026-04-13.

HHS's fiscal year 2027 Budget in Brief (release date per a law firm alert) proposes CDC budget authority of $5.280 billion (down $484 million from $5.764 billion), a National Center for Chemicals and Toxins in CDC, and moving CDC injury prevention, birth defects, chronic disease and HIV programs to the Administration for a Healthy America; the CDC chapter refers readers to the Office of Strategy chapter for the National Center for Health Statistics. An unverified lead from a post by the American Statistical Association (an association page) says HHS's justification proposes moving the center to the to-be-created Office of Strategy with $175.3 million, at low confidence; the Office of Strategy chapter text read gave no center-level breakdown.

The Rhode Island court (No. 25-cv-196) denies the government's motion to dismiss the amended complaint; all five counts (separation of powers, Appropriations Clause, ultra vires, and two APA counts) proceed. The order notes the First Circuit denied the government's emergency stay request on 2025-09-17 and that the government voluntarily dismissed its appeal of the preliminary injunction about six weeks later; it does not specifically address CDC.

title: Split CDC into a data-publishing agency and a separate public health policy agency
uncertainties: No proposal to split CDC into a data-publishing agency and a separate policy agency was found. The HHS Unified Agenda rule list on reginfo.gov (Agency Rule List - 2026) has five CDC entries, none on such a split, though a split would need legislation or a reorganization. The fiscal year 2027 request reportedly moves the National Center for Health Statistics to a new Office of Strategy; that rests on an unverified lead from one American Statistical Association post (low confidence); the Budget in Brief itself says only that the center is covered in the Office of Strategy chapter. The January 2026 claim that the final bill rejected major restructuring at CDC, HRSA, NIH and SAMHSA, and that the House passed the final agreement on 2026-01-22, is an unverified lead from an update by the National Coalition of STD Directors (an advocacy coalition), not confirmed by an official or news source; the Senate Appropriations Committee majority release dates the House's final passage of the bill to 2026-02-03. S. 999, in committee since 2025-03-12, would limit CDC authorities without creating a data agency. The 2025-07-01 injunction scope was not confirmed from its operative paragraphs. Diverged versus not_started is a judgment call. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
